channel.title: Shari Haley Bookkeeping blog
channel.description: Bookkeeping, QuickBooks, and tax-season answers for small businesses in DeLand and Volusia County, Florida.

item.title: Do I need a bookkeeper for my small business? 7 signs it’s time
item.description: Not sure if your small business needs a bookkeeper? Here are 7 common signs it’s time to get help, and what a bookkeeper actually does for you.

item.title: Bookkeeper vs. accountant vs. CPA: what’s the difference?
item.description: Bookkeepers, accountants, and CPAs do different jobs. Here’s what each one does, how they work together, and which ones your small business needs.

item.title: Behind on your books? What catch-up bookkeeping is and how it works
item.description: Months or years behind on your bookkeeping? Here’s what catch-up bookkeeping involves, what to gather, and how to stay current once you’re caught up.

item.title: Year-end bookkeeping checklist: get your books ready for tax season
item.description: A practical year-end bookkeeping checklist for small businesses: reconcile accounts, review payroll and 1099s, and hand your CPA clean books.

item.title: Should you learn QuickBooks yourself or hire a bookkeeper?
item.description: Weighing QuickBooks training against hiring a bookkeeper? Compare time, cost, and risk, and see when QuickBooks certification makes sense for your staff.

item.title: How long should a small business keep financial records?
item.description: How long to keep receipts, bank statements, and payroll records for your small business, based on IRS guidance, plus how to stay organized.

item.title: For CPAs: why referring clients to a dedicated bookkeeper makes tax season easier
item.description: For CPAs and tax pros in Volusia County: how a trusted bookkeeping referral partner means cleaner books, less cleanup, and a smoother tax season.

item.title: What a bookkeeper can (and can’t) do for your CPA firm’s clients
item.description: A clear division of labor for CPAs: what a bookkeeping partner handles for your clients, what stays with your firm, and how the year-end handoff works.
